# Brazil Coffee Case Validation for Food Systems Transition Group

## Recommendation

**Recommendation: validate further, but do not treat this as a mature Natural State / Nordic Circular Hotspot coffee case yet.** The strongest public evidence supports a **Brazil–Nordic circular economy link** around WCEF 2025 and a later **institutional reference to a signed partnership agreement** between Nordic Circular Hotspot and Exchange4Change covering, among other areas, **food systems**. However, I did **not** find a public MOU text, annex, meeting note, project file, pilot memo, or programme document that turns that into a **documented Brazil-coffee project** for Natural State / NCH. In other words: **“MOU/prosjektdokument ikke funnet” is a main finding.** citeturn7view0turn9search1turn14view0turn16view0

There **is** enough evidence to keep **Brazil coffee** alive as a **Norwegian import-value-chain / EUDR exposure case**. Norway’s sector association data shows Brazil is still the largest coffee origin in Norwegian imports, and institutional trade data for 2023 shows Norway imported substantial volumes of both unroasted and roasted coffee from Brazil. The EU’s EUDR regime clearly covers coffee, requires plot-level traceability for relevant commodities, and current official guidance says countries not specifically assigned another level are treated as **standard risk**; Brazil is **not** on the official low-risk or high-risk lists published by the Commission. That makes Brazil coffee a real compliance and traceability case, but **not yet a proven Natural State / NCH project case**. citeturn34search2turn20search15turn20search6turn22search1turn28view0turn29view2

**Recommended control status:** **`needs-actor-validation`** and **`needs-primary-check`**. If you need only one label, use **`needs-actor-validation`**. The case is **not** ready as `deckklart internt` in a fact-voice for a named Brazil coffee partnership/project, but it **is** solid enough for an internal hypothesis slide that says: *“Brazil coffee looks credible as a Norway/Nordics import-value-chain and EUDR case; public coffee-specific project documentation linking it to Natural State / NCH has not been found.”* citeturn7view0turn9search1turn16view0turn34search2turn31view0turn32view0

## Unsupported claims

The following claims should **not** be used in a deck or case card as if they were established facts.

| Ikke si | Why it is unsupported |
|---|---|
| “Natural State / NCH have a public Brazil coffee MOU.” | Public agreement text was not found. The best public evidence is only an institutional statement that a partnership agreement exists with Exchange4Change and includes food systems. citeturn16view0 |
| “WCEF 2025 launched a concrete Brazil coffee pilot for Nordic actors.” | The WCEF session only proves coffee was named as a use case in a discussion format. It does not prove a pilot. citeturn9search1 |
| “Fuglen was a documented partner in the Brazil/NCH/WCEF case.” | Fuglen is relevant as a Brazil sourcing actor, but I found no public source tying Fuglen to the reviewed Brazil/NCH/WCEF cooperation. citeturn10search0turn14view0 |
| “Norsk Kaffeinformasjon is a documented project partner in the Brazil case.” | NKI is a data owner / sector association in this review, not a documented Brazil project partner. citeturn34search2 |
| “Brazil is low-risk under EUDR.” | Current official list does not classify Brazil as low-risk; official guidance implies countries without another assignment are standard risk. citeturn28view0turn29view2 |
| “There is a validated Norwegian coffee-grounds biogas pilot linked to this case.” | I did not find a strong primary source for a named Norwegian coffee-grounds biogas pilot with volumes, facility and off-taker. citeturn47search2turn48search0 |
| “Coffee/EUDR sources prove partner role.” | They prove commodity exposure and compliance relevance, not partnership participation. citeturn22search1turn31view0turn12view0 |
